title: Grateful Dead Live at Kiel Auditorium on 1982-08-04
source: Source Info: Dan Healy's Master Soundboard Cassettes (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90/Dolby B)> Frank Streeter's 1st generation 1/4 track Reels @ 3.75 ips (Sony TC770/Maxell UD35-90B)> Tim Dalton's PCM (Sony SLHF400/Sony HG betamax tape); Transfer Info: PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch Pro > Tascam DA-3000 (wav 16-bit/44.1k)> Adobe Audition 3.0 > TLH flac16

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with frequent audience‑patch inserts still delivers a blues‑heavy set highlighted by Looks Like Rain, a Terrapin Station jam into Drums, and a rousing U.S. Blues encore.
ai_review.review: The show offers several inspired moments – the bluesy treatment of Looks Like Rain, an exploratory Terrapin Station → Drums sequence and a rocking U.S. Blues finale – and showcases Brent’s rare Yamaha electric‑grand piano work. The SBD source is marred by a very low Phil bass level and numerous audience‑patch splices that make the listening experience uneven, though the overall mix remains listenable.

ai_rating.rationale: One detailed 4‑star review points to a good musical performance with standout songs but notes significant recording issues (bass quiet, many audience patches), yielding an overall rating just above average.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Phil’s bass is unusually quiet; the tape contains many audience‑patch insertions that split up the flow, leading to occasional loss of clarity despite overall decent sound.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A mix of blues‑focused numbers and rockers with a strong second half; occasional X‑factor moments pop up despite some unevenness.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised as a perfect instrumental foil to Brent’s piano, indicating solid interplay.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass noted as far too quiet in the mix.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s Yamaha electric grand piano is highlighted as adept and uniquely expressive for this era.
